changed.title: Exact field-linear scan dimension for counting distinct affine-code words that satisfy local truth tables
changed.statement:
∀ (F : Type) [Field F] (k m t d : ℕ),
  let W := Fin k → ZMod 2
  ∀ (base : W) (gen : Fin m → W) (scope : Fin t → Finset (Fin k)),
    (∀ v : Fin k, ∃ j : Fin t, v ∈ scope j) →
    let key := fun a : Fin m → ZMod 2 => base + ∑ h : Fin m, a h • gen h
    let rk := fun S : Finset (Fin k) =>
      let M : Matrix (Fin m) S (ZMod 2) := fun row coord => gen row coord.val
      M.rank
    let need := (Finset.range (t+1)).sup (fun i =>
      let P := Finset.univ.filter (fun seen : Fin k => ∃ before : Fin t, before.val < i ∧ seen ∈ scope before)
      let Q := Finset.univ.filter (fun future : Fin k => ∃ after : Fin t, i ≤ after.val ∧ future ∈ scope after)
      2^(rk P + rk Q - rk Finset.univ))
    let T := fun idx : Fin t => (↥(scope idx) → ZMod 2) → Bool
    let count := fun tests : (j : Fin t) → T j =>
      Nat.card {w : W // w ∈ Set.range key ∧ ∀ j, tests j (fun tested => w tested.val) = true}
    (∃ (s : Fin d → F)
       (step : (j : Fin t) → T j → ((Fin d → F) →ₗ[F] (Fin d → F)))
       (out : (Fin d → F) →ₗ[F] F),
      ∀ tests : (j : Fin t) → T j,
        out ((List.finRange t).foldl (fun cur stage => step stage (tests stage) cur) s) =
          (count tests : F)) ↔ need ≤ d
changed.unlocks: Determines the exact linear memory for counting local tests restricted to a key code, including cuts with disjoint but correlated coordinate sets.
changed.context: Group legal prefixes by their sets of compatible suffixes. Each nonempty set is a coset of the future-only subcode. Equal or disjoint cosets give 2^(r(P)+r(Q)-r(all)) classes. Choose one word per class and pin its past and future projections by local singleton tables. The count matrix on these choices is an identity over every field and factors through the scan state. Conversely extend each class by feasible new coordinates, filter by the current table and add its prefix counts to the next classes. Initialize and finish with one class.

changed.title: Root counts give the exact syndrome frequencies for polynomial parity queries over a binary field
changed.statement:
∀ (k s r : ℕ), 0 < k → 0 < s → 0 < r →
  let F := ZMod 2
  let K := GaloisField 2 s
  let q := 2^s
  let V := Fin k → F
  let W := Fin s → F
  let R := Fin r → F
  ∀ (atPoint : Fin q ≃ K) (coord : K ≃ₗ[F] W) (a : Fin r → V) (t : R),
    let sample := fun (x : Fin q) (y : W) (j : Fin k) =>
      ∑ i : Fin s, y i * coord (atPoint x ^ j.val) i
    let hits := ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin q × W)).filter (fun z =>
      ∀ i : Fin r, (∑ j : Fin k, a i j * sample z.1 z.2 j) = t i)).card
    let roots := fun mask : R => ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin q)).filter (fun x =>
      coord (∑ j : Fin k, if (∑ i : Fin r, mask i * a i j) = 0 then (0 : K) else atPoint x ^ j.val) = (0 : W))).card
    (2:ℤ)^r * (hits : ℤ) =
      (q : ℤ) * ∑ mask : R,
        (if (∑ i : Fin r, mask i*t i) = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1) * (roots mask : ℤ) ∧
    (LinearIndependent F a → q^2 ≤ 2^r*hits + 2^(r-1)*q*(k-1))
changed.unlocks: Gives an explicit field query list for the three-test density condition.
changed.context: Use the character filter of the syndrome. For fixed x and mask c, summing over y cancels unless the masked polynomial vanishes at x. At a root all q signs are positive. This gives the exact formula for dependent checks as well. The zero mask contributes q². With independent checks every nonzero mask polynomial is nonzero of degree at most k−1. For nonzero t exactly 2^(r−1) masks have negative signs. For zero t none do. Bound each negative contribution by q(k−1).

changed.title: Equal sums of dyadic masses admit a partition with bounded leaf offsets over distinct root exponents
changed.statement:
∀ (m s : ℕ) (leaf : Fin m → ℕ) (root : Fin s → ℕ), Function.Injective root →
  (((∑ i : Fin m, (1 : ℚ) / 2 ^ (leaf i)) =
    ∑ j : Fin s, (1 : ℚ) / 2 ^ (root j)) ↔
    ∃ (group : Fin m → Fin s) (offset : Fin m → Fin m),
      (∀ i, leaf i = root (group i) + (offset i).val) ∧
      ∀ j : Fin s,
        (∑ i ∈ (Finset.univ.filter (fun k : Fin m => group k = j)),
          2 ^ (m - (offset i).val) : ℕ) = 2 ^ m)
changed.unlocks: Splits any exact dyadic sum over distinct exponents into weight-one blocks of bounded offset, the step that turns attainable clause densities into finitely many affine shapes.
changed.context: Merge two equal depths into their parent, tracking each original leaf and increasing its offset by one whenever its block moves. The root sum is less than two, so a pair at depth zero never occurs. At most m-1 merges occur when m is positive. Distinct-root dyadic expansions are unique by parity after multiplying by the largest occurring denominator. Match the surviving roots to the given roots. Each block has normalized weight one. Conversely group the sum and scale each block by its root mass.

changed.title: Interior gates save at most half a gate apiece when decoding every choice of one literal per pair
changed.statement:
∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r →
  let I := Fin (2 * r)
  let names := fun (x : Fin (2 ^ r)) =>
    Finset.univ.filter (fun i : I => Nat.testBit x.val (i.val / 2) = decide (i.val % 2 = 1))
  let supp := fun (E : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (w : ℕ) =>
    Finset.univ.filter (fun i : I =>
      (E.wires (List.ofFn (fun h : I => decide (h = i)))).getD w false = true)
  let realizes := fun (E : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    ∀ x : Fin (2 ^ r), ∃ w : ℕ, supp E w = names x
  ∀ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, realizes C →
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or → g.inputs.length ≤ 2) →
    let price := fun (p : Fin C.gates.length) =>
      let S := supp C (2 * r + p.val)
      @ite ℕ ((C.gates.get p).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or)
        (Classical.propDecidable _) 2 (if (∃ x, S ⊆ names x) then
        (if S.card = 2 then 2 else if 3 ≤ S.card then 3 else 0)
      else 0)
    ∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, realizes D ∧
      (∀ g ∈ D.gates, g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or ∧ g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
      2 * D.size ≤ ∑ p, price p
changed.unlocks: Prices interior gates on the literal-input decoder in the signed selector search and rules out a one-gate saving from one such gate on that side.
changed.context: For each target cut its backward OR paths at other gates. Choose one outgoing edge per vertex and one source for each literal. Prune to a binary tree on disjoint leaf blocks. Complete each block of h literals by a binary tree, charging each branch 2^(leaf count). The cheapest full tree builds all targets by joining both subfamilies. An OR averages at most one over targets. A cut of support size t fits at most 2^(r-t) targets. Completion costs zero for h<=1, four for h=2 and at most 3*2^h/2 otherwise by splitting evenly after checking h=3,4,5. Double the average.

changed.title: Conditional sign-matrix rank and rigidity from triangular Walsh support and coefficient formulas
changed.statement:
let triangularSupport : Prop :=
  ∀ t : ℕ,
    let V := Fin t → ZMod 2
    ∀ (A B : Fin t → Fin t → ZMod 2) (γ : V),
      let sources := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin t)).filter (fun j =>
        ∃ i, j < i ∧ (A i j ≠ 0 ∨ B i j ≠ 0))
      let c := fun (j : Fin t) (z : V × V) =>
        γ j + ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ioi j, (z.1 i * A i j + z.2 i * B i j)
      let live := (Finset.univ : Finset (V × V)).filter (fun z =>
        ∀ j, c j z ≠ 0 ∨ (z.1 j = 0 ∧ z.2 j = 0))
      let lhs := 2 * 4^sources.card * live.card
      let rhs := (4^sources.card + 1) * 4^t
      lhs ≤ rhs ∧
        (lhs = rhs ↔
          (∀ j, j ∉ sources → γ j = 1) ∧
          ∀ j ∈ sources, ∀ k ∈ sources, ∀ z, c j z = c k z)
let coefficientProduct : Prop :=
  ∀ s : ℕ,
    let V := Fin s → ZMod 2
    let dot := fun (u v : V) => ∑ i : Fin s, u i * v i
    let sign := fun (x : ZMod 2) => if x = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1
    ∀ (A B : Fin s → Fin s → ZMod 2) (γ : V) (Z : V → V → V),
    (∀ x y i, Z x y i =
      (x i + ∑ j ∈ Finset.Iio i, A i j * Z x y j) *
      (y i + ∑ j ∈ Finset.Iio i, B i j * Z x y j)) →
    ∀ p q : V,
      let c := fun (j : Fin s) =>
        γ j + ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ioi j, (p i * A i j + q i * B i j)
      (∑ x : V, ∑ y : V, sign (dot γ (Z x y) + dot p x + dot q y)) =
        ∏ j : Fin s,
          if c j = 0 then (if p j = 0 ∧ q j = 0 then 4 else 0)
          else 2 * sign (p j * q j)
let conclusion : Prop :=
  let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
    (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
    xor (xor (g.op.eval [false,false]) (g.op.eval [false,true]))
        (xor (g.op.eval [true,false]) (g.op.eval [true,true]))
  ∀ (n m : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) →
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n+m) C →
    let t := C.gates.countP nonlinear
    let raw := Fin (n+m) → Bool
    let W := fun (w : ℕ) (x : raw) => (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD w false
    let defect : Matrix (Fin (n+m+C.gates.length)) (raw × raw) (ZMod 2) := fun w v =>
      if (∃ g ∈ C.gates, nonlinear g = true ∧ w.val ∈ g.inputs) ∧
        xor (xor (W w.val v.1) (W w.val v.2))
            (xor (W w.val (fun i => xor (v.1 i) (v.2 i))) (W w.val (fun _ => false))) = true
      then 1 else 0
    let value := fun (a : Fin n) (b : Fin m) => C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach a b)
    let K : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) ℚ := fun i j => if value i j then -1 else 1
    let V := Fin (2*t) → ZMod 2
    2 * 4^defect.rank * K.rank ≤ (4^defect.rank + 1) * 4^t ∧
    (5 * 4^t < 8 * K.rank → defect.rank = 0 ∧
      ∃ (row : Fin n → V) (col : Fin m → V) (Q : Fin n → Bool) (R : Fin m → Bool),
        ∀ i j, value i j = xor (xor (Q i) (R j))
          (decide ((∑ b : Fin (2*t), row i b * col j b) = 1)))
triangularSupport → coefficientProduct → conclusion

changed.context: Introduce the displayed hypotheses. Write each operand as a raw affine term plus earlier formal products. Its four-value additivity defect is the same combination of the earlier product defects, so r is bounded by the count d of products feeding later gates. On the promise, the sign table selects rows and columns of the full XOR decoder up to signs. Its rational rank is bounded by the Walsh support. Apply the source bound. Above 5/8 no source is possible, and an omitted final product kills 3/4. Polarize the surviving disjoint products. Allow 180 to 300 minutes.

changed.title: A clause supported on a variable set eliminates its full squarefree monomial (known result rebuilt)
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (C : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)),
  S.Nonempty → (C.image Prod.fst) ⊆ S →
  (∀ i : Fin n, ¬ ((i, true) ∈ C ∧ (i, false) ∈ C)) →
  PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PCDerivable (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.cnfSystem F) S.card (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.clausePoly C) →
  ∃ q : MvPolynomial (Fin n) (ZMod 2), q.totalDegree < S.card ∧
    PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PCDerivable (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.cnfSystem F) S.card ((∏ i ∈ S, MvPolynomial.X i) + q)
changed.unlocks: Supplies the squarefree reduction required to build the support-covering quotient.
changed.context: Multiply the derived clause polynomial by the product of the variables of S outside the clause. The nonzero clause polynomial has degree equal to its support size, and the new factors are all distinct. The product has the full S-monomial as its unique term of degree |S| with coefficient one. Cancel that term to define the lower-degree polynomial. Each intermediate multiplication fits the same degree budget.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt: conditional binary source coding with less than one bit of redundancy
changed.statement:
∀ (m h : ℕ) (w : Fin h → ℝ) (p : Fin h → Fin m → ℝ),
  (∀ y, 0 < w y) → (∑ y, w y) = 1 →
  (∀ y i, 0 < p y i) → (∀ y, (∑ i, p y i) = 1) →
  let prefixCode := fun (code : Fin m → List Bool) =>
    ∀ i j, (∃ tail : List Bool, code j = code i ++ tail) → i = j
  let H := ∑ y, w y * (∑ i, p y i * (-Real.log (p y i) / Real.log 2))
  let cost := fun (code : Fin h → Fin m → List Bool) =>
    ∑ y, w y * (∑ i, p y i * ((code y i).length : ℝ))
  (∀ code, (∀ y, prefixCode (code y)) → H ≤ cost code) ∧
    ∃ code, (∀ y, prefixCode (code y)) ∧ cost code < H+1
changed.unlocks: Bounds mean description length when the decoder sees a condition.
changed.context: A shorter mean than the entropy cannot exist by the Kraft bound and relative entropy. For each condition take ceiling minus log2 probability as the lengths. Kraft gives a prefix code, including length zero for a singleton. For any competitor normalize its dyadic masses by their sum and apply nonnegativity of relative entropy, using the Kraft bound. Multiply each conditional inequality by the condition weight and sum. Estimated 90 minutes.

  let prefixCode := fun (code : Fin m → List Bool) =>
    ∀ i j, (∃ tail : List Bool, code j = code i ++ tail) → i = j
  ∃ code, prefixCode code ∧
    (∀ i j, i < j → List.Lex (fun a b : Bool => a = false ∧ b = true) (code i) (code j)) ∧

changed.title: Known result rebuilt: Shtarkov minimax regret for a finite model with binary prefix rounding
changed.statement:
∀ (m h : ℕ) (p : Fin h → Fin m → ℝ) (e : Fin m → ℝ), 0 < m → 0 < h →
  (∀ j i, 0 < p j i) → (∀ j, (∑ i, p j i) = 1) →
  (∀ i, (∀ j, p j i ≤ e i) ∧ ∃ j, p j i = e i) →
  let prefixCode := fun (code : Fin m → List Bool) =>
    ∀ i j, (∃ tail : List Bool, code j = code i ++ tail) → i = j
  let Z := ∑ i, e i
  (∀ i j, p j i ≤ Z*(e i/Z)) ∧ (∑ i, e i/Z) = 1 ∧
  (∀ q : Fin m → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 < q i) → (∑ i, q i) = 1 →
    ∃ i j, Z*q i ≤ p j i) ∧
  (∀ c, prefixCode c → ∃ i j, Z ≤ p j i * (2:ℝ)^(c i).length) ∧
  ∃ c, prefixCode c ∧ ∀ i j, p j i * (2:ℝ)^(c i).length < 2*Z

If all envelope entries were below Z times a competitor, summing would contradict its normalization. Choose a model attaining the offending entry. The same sum argument uses Kraft for a prefix code. Shannon rounding for the normalized envelope loses strictly less than a factor of two. Estimated 90 minutes.

changed.title: How often can one affine map recover a designated endpoint from the two marked positions?
changed.statement:
∀ n : Nat, 0 < n →
  let V := Fin n → ZMod 2
  let unit := fun (i j : Fin n) => if j = i then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0
  let arc := fun (c : V) (z : Fin n → V) (i j : Fin n) =>
    i ≠ j ∧ c + z i + z j = unit i
  let total := fun (c : V) (z : Fin n → V) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n × Fin n)).filter (fun p => arc c z p.1 p.2)).card
  let m := n - 1 + (n - 1)^2 / 4
  (∀ c z, total c z ≤ m) ∧ (∃ c z, total c z = m) ∧
    ∀ c z, total c z = m →
      ∃ (t : Fin n) (A : Finset (Fin n)), t ∉ A ∧ A.card = (n-1)/2 ∧
        (∀ i, i ≠ t → arc c z t i ∨ arc c z i t) ∧
        ∀ i j, i ≠ t → j ≠ t → i ≠ j →
          ((arc c z i j ∨ arc c z j i) ↔ ((i ∈ A ∧ j ∉ A) ∨ (i ∉ A ∧ j ∈ A)))
changed.unlocks: Supplies the one-map maximum and its equality structure for the three-map obstruction.
changed.context: Each successful unordered edge has one orientation. XOR the three outputs of a useful triangle. Column terms cancel, leaving the bias, whose odd support is nonempty and lies in the triangle. Delete any support vertex, or any vertex if there are no triangles. The remainder is triangle-free. For maximum degree d on N vertices its edges number at most (N-d)d, with equality only for complete balanced bipartite extremizers. Attain the bound using a middle vertex t, bias e_t, columns e_t+e_i on one side and zero at t and on the other side.

changed.title: The 7 by 7 crown (u joined to v when u and v differ): some AND/OR circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 22 gates represents it
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun u v : Fin 7 => decide (u ≠ v)) 22
changed.unlocks: the crown ladder: whether one crown beats our held circuit at n = 7
changed.context: Answer with a circuit: a gate list (AND or OR, at most two wires read; wires 0 to 6 left, 7 to 13 right, gate j writes wire 14+j, each gate reads only earlier wires) and the output wire, judged on all 49 inputs with one vertex on each side. We hold 23 gates: one OR of the two vertex wires per index, then two-of-7 on those ORs by a prefix chain, 4n - 5 (computed). The 5 by 5 crown is exactly 15 and the 6 by 6 needs at least 18, both checked. We do not know whether 22 exists.
changed.shard_spec:
0: at most 22 gates in all, with at most 3 AND gates.
1: at most 22 gates in all, with 4 to 6 AND gates.
2: at most 22 gates in all, with 7 to 10 AND gates.
3: at most 22 gates in all, with at least 11 AND gates.
